properties.name: OS
properties.description: The Oncology Sales (OS) Representative is a customer-facing commercial professional responsible for engaging healthcare professionals (HCPs) to communicate approved product information, understand customer needs, support the appropriate use of approved products within the approved indication, and build professional relationships through compliant promotional interactions. The OS Representative discusses approved product information, clinical evidence, efficacy, safety within promotional scope, treatment positioning, patient identification opportunities, customer feedback, and competitive insights while adhering to commercial and regulatory guidelines.

properties.name: FRM
properties.description: The Field Reimbursement Manager (FRM) is a customer-facing commercial professional responsible for helping healthcare providers and healthcare accounts overcome reimbursement and patient access challenges for approved products. The FRM provides education on payer requirements, reimbursement processes, access resources, and approved reimbursement support services to facilitate appropriate patient access while remaining compliant with commercial, legal, and regulatory guidelines.

properties.name: PHI/PII protection
properties.summary: Exclude Protected Health Information, PII, and any patient-identifying details from summaries.

properties.name: Medical Information Request capture
properties.summary: Capture MIRs only as administrative interactions (ID, neutral topic, response method, triage status) without clinical content.

properties.name: Toxicity language control
properties.summary: Replace the word 'toxicity' with 'safety concerns' in generated call summaries.

properties.text: Building and maintaining professional relationships with oncologists, hematologists, advanced practice providers, pharmacists, nurses, and other relevant healthcare professionals.

Conducting compliant scientific and promotional discussions regarding approved products, including indication, efficacy, safety, dosing, administration, and appropriate patient selection within the approved label.
Understanding HCP treatment practices, prescribing behavior, clinical preferences, and educational needs related to approved products.
Identifying opportunities for appropriate product utilization based on customer discussions and approved product positioning.

Discussing approved product information, including indications, clinical evidence, efficacy, safety within promotional scope, dosing, administration, patient identification, treatment positioning, and appropriate use of approved products.
Addressing customer questions within promotional scope and facilitating appropriate follow-up through Medical Affairs or other internal partners when discussions extend beyond promotional boundaries.
Gathering customer insights regarding HCP clinical practice, treatment preferences, customer feedback, educational needs, and competitive landscape within the promotional scope of approved products.

Collaborating with cross-functional partners (such as Medical Science Liaisons, FRM, KAM, and other internal stakeholders) to support customer needs while remaining within defined functional responsibilities.
Identifying opportunities for appropriate product utilization based on HCP discussions regarding approved product use and customer needs.
Planning and executing customer engagements aligned with territory objectives and customer priorities.
Documenting customer interactions accurately and compliantly.

Exclude all adverse event, safety, protocol-related, toxicity management, administration protocol, and clinical management discussions from the summary. Such information is outside the Oncology Sales (OS) commercial scope and should not be shared with commercial field members. If appeared in the call summary, treat it only as information requiring appropriate reporting or routing per policy, without summarizing or referencing the clinical content.
properties.reason: outside the Oncology Sales (OS) commercial scope and should not be shared with commercial field members.

properties.text: Building and maintaining relationships with reimbursement specialists, office staff, practice administrators, patient access teams, financial counselors, specialty pharmacies, and other stakeholders involved in reimbursement and patient access.

Educating healthcare accounts on payer coverage policies, reimbursement processes, prior authorization requirements, benefits verification, claims and appeals processes, specialty pharmacy coordination, and approved reimbursement and patient support resources.

Gathering customer insights specifically related to reimbursement processes, payer requirements, coverage policies, prior authorization status, benefits verification outcomes, affordability considerations, and patient access experiences â€” documented instances include payer coverage decisions, reimbursement barriers, access challenges, and patient support program utilization.
Adherence to clinical treatment protocols, medication adherence strategies, and mitigation protocol education are NOT FRM insights and must not be included.

Identifying reimbursement and patient access barriers affecting appropriate access to approved products and discussing approved reimbursement resources, payer support services, financial assistance programs, reimbursement tools, and patient access resources that facilitate appropriate access to approved products.

Documenting reimbursement-related discussions, payer policy updates, reimbursement determinations, patient access challenges, approved support resources discussed, agreed actions, and reimbursement follow-up activities arising from customer interactions.

Gathering and documenting discussions related to patient support resources (e.g., copay assistance, patient assistance programs, caregiver financial support), office reimbursement workflows (e.g., billing processes, claims submission), affordability programs, and access-facilitation resources â€” documented instances include discussions about specific support programs available, enrollment processes, and affordability barriers.
Patient education materials, clinical adherence education, and treatment protocol guidance are NOT FRM patient support discussions and must not be included.

Supporting healthcare accounts in understanding reimbursement processes, navigating patient access pathways, utilizing approved patient support resources, and addressing reimbursement or coverage-related questions through approved education.

Coordinating with cross-functional partners (e.g., OS, KAM, MSL, OCE, PMAM, UBAM, Market Access, and Patient Support teams) only when customer needs extend beyond the FRM's functional responsibilities, and including cross-functional or clinical-operational coordination details only when they directly relate to reimbursement, coverage, prior authorization, affordability, or patient access workflows.
If a call contains no in-scope reimbursement/access facts, record no FRM insight for that call.

Excluding adverse event, safety, protocol-related, toxicity management, administration protocol, and other clinical management discussions from the summary. These topics are outside the FRM commercial scope and should be handled by the appropriate medical function in accordance with organizational policy.
properties.reason: outside the FRM commercial scope and should be handled by the appropriate medical function in accordance with organizational policy.

properties.text: Gathering facts using only reimbursement, patient access, payer coverage, affordability, and patient financial support facts.
Office operational facts are only in scope when they directly describe a reimbursement or access workflow (e.g., how billing is submitted, how prior authorization is processed).
Never include clinical operational workflows (e.g., electronic ordering systems, prophylaxis drop-down menus, EHR treatment ordering).

Ignore all facts related to clinical treatment preferences, product efficacy, prescribing preferences, biomarker testing, disease-state education, therapeutic decision-making, medication adherence protocols, or mitigation strategies.

properties.barrier_details: They are seeing very few eligible patients right now, so the team is not confident they can operationalize the pathway consistently. They asked for a simple way to recognize and flag potential candidates as they appear.
properties.account_ask: A simple way to recognize and flag potential candidates as they appear.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Given the difficulty operationalizing the pathway at Apollo Hospitals, did you and {hcp} discuss implementing a streamlined criteria or flagging tool to identify candidates as they appear?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Regarding account pathway operations at Apollo Hospitals: historical feedback noted seeing few eligible patients and needing a simple way to operationalize the pathway. Did {hcp} or the team mention any friction identifying or flagging eligible candidates today?

properties.barrier_details: Biomarker testing and/or results are sometimes delayed, which slows down patient identification in their pathway. The team asked to align internally on where testing fits in their workflow and who owns tracking results.
properties.account_ask: Align internally on where testing fits in their workflow and who owns tracking results.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Regarding the biomarker testing delays at Fortis Healthcare, did you and the team align internally on where testing fits in their clinical workflow and who owns tracking the results?
properties.case_2_inquiry: In terms of clinical workflow, Fortis Healthcare previously experienced biomarker testing turnaround delays. Did {hcp} mention whether testing delays are currently impacting patient identification, or who tracks the results?

properties.barrier_details: Key steps in their diagnosis-to-treatment pathway are taking longer than expected due to scheduling and coordination, which delays next-step decisions. The team wants clearer handoffs so potential candidates are identified and routed sooner.
properties.account_ask: Clearer handoffs so potential candidates are identified and routed sooner.
properties.case_1_inquiry: With diagnosis-to-treatment scheduling delays at Manipal Hospitals, did you and the team establish clearer handoffs so potential candidates can be identified and routed sooner?
properties.case_2_inquiry: At Manipal Hospitals, scheduling and coordination across the diagnosis-to-treatment pathway have previously delayed next-step decisions. Did {hcp} mention any scheduling friction or need for clearer candidate routing handoffs today?

properties.barrier_details: There are delays in the diagnostic workup and internal handoffs, so potential candidates are identified late in the process. The team wants a cleaner pathway with fewer missed handoffs between roles.
properties.account_ask: A cleaner pathway with fewer missed handoffs between roles.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Given the diagnostic workup delays at Max Healthcare, did you discuss creating a cleaner pathway with fewer missed handoffs between diagnostic and clinical roles?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Regarding workflow coordination, Max Healthcare has previously seen diagnostic workup delays and late candidate identification. Did {hcp} mention any internal handoff friction or missed handoffs between roles today?

properties.barrier_details: The site is not consistently identifying potential candidates in their current workflow. They want a simple way to flag appropriate patients earlier without adding extra burden to clinic staff.
properties.account_ask: A simple way to flag appropriate patients earlier without adding extra burden to clinic staff.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Given that candidate identification has been inconsistent at Narayana Health, did you explore a simplified way to flag appropriate patients earlier without burdening clinic staff?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Narayana Health has previously sought an easier way to flag eligible candidates earlier without adding burden to clinic staff. Did patient identification or workflow burden come up during your discussion today?

properties.barrier_details: PA turnaround times are inconsistent, which makes it hard for the team to plan next steps. They asked to use approved access-support resources to understand the process and reduce rework.
properties.account_ask: Use approved access-support resources to understand the process and reduce rework.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Given the inconsistent PA turnaround times at Apollo Hospitals, did you review approved access-support resources with the team to clarify payer requirements and reduce rework?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Before we finalize, Apollo Hospitals previously faced inconsistent PA turnaround times. Did the team raise any prior authorization turnaround delays or ask to use approved access-support resources today?

properties.barrier_details: Patient cost exposure is a concern and the team wants clearer expectations before moving forward. They asked about benefits verification and approved resources that can help set expectations appropriately.
properties.account_ask: Benefits verification and approved resources that can help set expectations appropriately.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Regarding the patient cost exposure concerns at Fortis Healthcare, did you discuss benefits verification steps and approved affordability resources to establish clear expectations?
properties.case_2_inquiry: A key operational consideration at Fortis Healthcare has been patient cost exposure. Did benefits verification, copay support, or patient cost expectations come up during your meeting?

properties.barrier_details: Prior authorization timelines are creating scheduling uncertainty. The account asked what information their payer typically requests and wanted support using the appropriate, approved access pathway to reduce back-and-forth.
properties.account_ask: What information their payer typically requests and support using the appropriate, approved access pathway to reduce back-and-forth.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Regarding the PA scheduling uncertainty at Manipal Hospitals, did you clarify typical payer documentation requests and guide the team on using the approved access pathway to reduce back-and-forth?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Prior authorization timelines have created scheduling uncertainty at Manipal Hospitals in the past. Did the account ask about typical payer clinical requirements or need access pathway support to reduce back-and-forth?

properties.barrier_details: The product is not on the current formulary (or is restricted), so usage requires an exception pathway. The account needs clarity on committee timing, required documentation, and who will submit the request.
properties.account_ask: Clarity on committee timing, required documentation, and who will submit the request.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Since the product requires a formulary exception at Max Healthcare, did you clarify P&T committee timing, the required clinical documentation package, and who will submit the request?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Regarding institutional access at Max Healthcare, since the brand requires a formulary exception pathway, did you discuss committee timing, required documentation, or who will submit the request?

properties.barrier_details: Recent changes in payer coverage policy created uncertainty about requirements and next steps. The account requested the latest available, published policy information and clarity on how to route questions through the approved access support channel.
properties.account_ask: The latest available, published policy information and clarity on how to route questions through the approved access support channel.
properties.case_1_inquiry: Regarding the recent payer policy changes impacting Narayana Health, did you share the latest published coverage policy guidelines and explain how to route questions through the approved access support channel?
properties.case_2_inquiry: Recent payer coverage policy changes have created uncertainty at Narayana Health. Did the team request updated published policy guidelines or ask how to route questions through approved access support channels?
